text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Set the focus ring to 3px wide with 7:1 contrast and NO animation. This meets WCAG 2.2 AA for focus indicators while respecting reduced-motion preferences. The 3px width is large enough for visibility but small enough to avoid obscuring content. The 7:1 contrast ensures readability for low-vision users without relying on color alone. Trade-off: slightly less visible than a thicker ring, but avoids motion that can trigger vestibular disorders.

name: Reader
text: A 3px ring still risks losing users who rely on motion to track focus—especially those with vestibular disorders or attention deficits. A better alternative: a 2px ring with a 3:1 contrast fallback for reduced-motion, paired with a subtle 1px offset animation *only* when motion is enabled. Settle it with user testing: measure task completion time for keyboard users with and without motion.

name: Ramp
text:
Set the focus ring to 2px wide with 3:1 contrast by default, and add a 1px offset pulse animation *only* when reduced-motion is disabled. This keeps the ring visible for most users while avoiding harm to those with vestibular disorders. The trade-off is slightly lower visibility for some users, but it prevents exclusion of a vulnerable group—motion sensitivity is a recognized disability under WCAG.

name: Reader
text: A 2px ring at 3:1 contrast fails WCAG 2.2 AA for focus indicators—it’s too faint for low-vision users. The real risk is locking out people who need high contrast, not just motion cues. Settle it by testing both rings with keyboard users who rely on focus visibility, not assumptions.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Finalize 3px focus ring at 7:1 contrast, 1px outer stroke, NO animation. Deliver: focus ring spec + test results with 3 keyboard users. Owner: Ramp.
